industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the sector rows doing the work: Renewable energy equipment and Test and measurement go to D this week and Electrical equipment, Flow control and Building technology hold D, against Distributors, Diversified groups, Engineered components and Industrial services at C. Danske (26-Nov) has automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries) as data-centre installers peak (Bravida Sell; Kristell, 22-Nov) and Kepler (26-Nov) likes cables (Prysmian) and testing; Goldman's cyclical call names Technology, Retailers and Aerospace and Defence, not capital goods. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Three live holdings (Arteche, IMCD, Sdiptech; 12.93 points). Counter-case for D: the tape and the capital-spending unwind; for B: the automation turn. To D on relative strength F with a hyperscaler guide cut read.

sector.key: O.4. Electrical equipment, grid and automation
sector.why: Underweight, carried; the condition to F (a hyperscaler guide cut read in the sources) has not fired and the condition back to C (relative strength leaving F with a dated capital-spending read intact) is not met: relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior), the third F. The AI capital-spending read turned this week (surplus evidence; Garran, Menon) while Kepler (Donneky, 26-Nov) notes Prysmian still winning hyperscaler deals with data-centre work at 12% of sales, so the grid-as-bottleneck case survives at the second order. One live holding, Arteche (3.02%, Thematic Fit/Momentum F, Bottom-up 91.4), the model exception judged in component 5. No Pool name. Counter-case: the grid is the physical bottleneck of the largest capital-spending theme and Arteche's Sell-side Momentum reads A. Back to C if relative strength leaves F with a dated grid-order read; to F on a hyperscaler guide cut read in the sources.

geography.why: Overweight, carried: the 15% inclusive US tariff on Switzerland is 'largely as expected' (Goldman, 25-Nov), Roche is Kepler's pharma top pick and 'the clear AI leader in pharma' (26-Nov), and the Swiss market's low-beta character is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank and the franc were not read. Counter-case: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
